scope: Proposition 10.1 (Regular minimal cap) of the manuscript “Purely cosmetic surgery on knots in the three-sphere” (preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 306 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ee916c92b825a868), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 129. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: At each of finitely many regular isolated main-component limits on a trace face, the cap data can be chosen arbitrarily small, compatibly with the preceding exclusions, so that the following statements hold. The framed cap problem of charge 1/4, with its sphere-sweep mark and the normalized holonomy condition −1, is a finite set of regular points. Every point is a crossing on the unique harmonic Abelian connection with ordered summand difference v(S) = 2. These points are fixed by H, and their oriented sum has absolute value one. The spinor is zero, and the coupled Dirac operator is invertible at each point. The choices for the two determinant lifts are related by the prescribed cap tensor operation.
